newsitem.title: USA: NY Legislature passes low-cost power for jobs bill.
newsitem.headline: NY Legislature passes low-cost power for jobs bill.

text.p: The New York State Senate and Assembly Tuesday passed legislation that will make low-cost power available to businesses in New York state to encourage job retention and expansion.
The legislation reflects the work of a Joint Legislative Conference Committee, which earlier reached an agreement on the legislation earlier Tuesday.
"The low-cost power will be an aggressive tool for us to lower energy costs to protect and create jobs," Senate Majority Leader Joseph L. Bruno said.
Senator James Seward, chairman of the Senate Energy and Telecommunications Committee said the legislation will make 400 megawatts of low-cost power available.

The power will be provided by the state Power Authority and through a competitive bid process. The program will be paid for through a credit against the Gross Receipts Tax and a contribution from the New York Power Authority.
"Now we have a model for competition" in power supplies, according to Paul Larrrabee, a spokesman for Assemblyman Paul Tonko, chairman of the Assembly Energy Committee.
